ledger_truncation.note: Rows for steps trained after the last checkpoint are discarded on resume; their weights were discarded too, so counting their tokens would be a lie.
ledger_truncation.scope: Row-level ledgers are truncated exactly. The learning ledger's running aggregates (per-shard, per-role, per-document sums) are rebuilt from the retained rows going forward rather than restored, because a resumed process re-derives them from the ledger file. At demo scale that re-derivation is skipped; a production system would fold the retained rows back into the accumulators here.

what_this_is: A checkpoint is saved, training continues, the run state is destroyed, and the run is rebuilt from the checkpoint and re-trained over the same steps. Bitwise weight equality is the claim; ledger row equality is the proof it was the same data in the same order.
